Okay, thank you for the reminder.

Please grok how versioning is handled.  You've currently just added this property to OpenBMCManager.v1_0_0.Fan, which means there will now be two different versions that report 1.0.0.

You need to create a 1.1.0 version, inherit from 1.0.0, and update to use the new version.  There are many examples of this in the DMTF schemas.

once more, C++ core guidelines for function size.

I feel like one way this could be simplified is to perform 2 steps

first step: query D-Bus and put the result into some kind of struct
second step: convert that struct to json

Another way this could be simplified is to extract the lambda from line 66 and put it as a separate function. That would already reduce the indentation.

Another way is to extract the inner part of a loop into a separate function.


Overall, it is not clear to me how and by which maintainer we got to the point of having this enormous function...

I had started the refactoring on this a while ago here:
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/88962

I've restacked the patches so that this makes more sense.  Let me know if anyone objects, and if not I'll squash it into this review.
Acknowledged

please look into C++ core guidelines on function length.

This function is already way too long and the patch is not helping there.
outdated comment, patch has changed and this comment no longer applies.

```
The wrong BaseType meant v1_1_0.Manager started fresh from the generic OData root rather than inheriting from v1_0_0.Manager — silently dropping Certificates. The runtime code in openbmc_managers.hpp was also updated in the same commit to emit "@odata.type": "#OpenBMCManager.v1_1_0.Manager", so the RSV immediately validated all OEM properties against the broken new type and hit the unknown-property failure on Certificates.
```
